05 · How it’s built

One metric, shown all the way down, because the number has to survive a Finance review

Nobody in HR software shows you their definitions. Here is ours for voluntary attrition, as it runs tonight.

-- metrics/attrition_voluntary_rate.sql · v1 · ISO 30414 turnover rate
-- Runs nightly in Airflow. Versioned. Same inputs, same number.

with exits as (
  select employee_id, exit_date
  from mart.fct_employee_events
  where event_type = 'exit'
    and exit_reason in ('resignation', 'absconded')      -- voluntary only
    and exit_date between :period_start and :period_end
),
headcount as (
  select avg(active_headcount) as avg_headcount
  from mart.fct_daily_headcount
  where day between :period_start and :period_end
),
scoped as (
  select e.*, o.team_id, o.zone_id
  from exits e join mart.dim_org o using (employee_id)
)
select
  team_id,
  case when avg_headcount < 10 then null            -- withheld under DPDP policy
       else count(*)::numeric / avg_headcount end   as attrition_voluntary_rate,
  count(*)                                           as exits,
  avg_headcount
from scoped cross join headcount
group by team_id, avg_headcount;

The rule, in plain language

What counts
Resignations and absconding. Not terminations, contract ends, deaths or internal transfers.
Denominator
Average active headcount over the period, not opening headcount. Finance signs this off once.
Withheld
Any team under 10 people shows as withheld, never as a number.
Versioned
v1 since 14 Aug 2026. A definition change is a new version, so last quarter’s number never moves.
Open source
Postgres, Airflow, dbt Core and Soda checks. The code sits in your repository.

Inside your walls

Deployed in your own cloud, served from India. Anvaya™ runs inside your account, in your region. We never host your data.

DPDP-compliant by design. Per-tenant isolation, row-level access, a consent ledger in Sangam, and identity checks through Setu so Aadhaar and PAN never sit in the system.

What the design covers, and what stays with you →

What we refuse to build

  • ✕A dashboard nobody opens. We send the brief where people already read.
  • ✕A model that sees an employee record. It sees masked sentences, never the row.
  • ✕A saving claimed without a holdout. No comparison group, no number.
  • ✕A number that changes between runs. Definitions are versioned and precalculated.
  • ✕Lock-in. Open source underneath, deployed in your cloud, the code is yours.
